title: 01. Confirm the CDK constructs exist in the pinned version
body:
**Type:** AFK  
**Slice:** 01

## Parent PRD

`.scratch/wayfinder/poll-app/spec.md` (decision map: `map.md`; ordered plan: `build-plan.md`; compute decision: ADR 0001)

## What to build

Local synth and docs checks, no AWS resources. The research read `aws-cdk-lib` 2.273.0 docs but the repo pins 2.260.0, and several decisions depend on specific constructs. Find out now what exists, before building on it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The pinned version is checked for each of these, and the exact API names are recorded as a comment on this issue: the Function URL origin with origin access control; asset directories that follow symlinks; the log-delivery resources (destination, source, delivery) and the property that selects JSON output; Glue table, Athena workgroup and named query constructs; saved Logs Insights query definitions; the Lambda runtime constant to use.
- [ ] A throwaway synth confirms that asset content hashes appear in the template for a Lambda code asset and a bucket deployment.
- [ ] Node is confirmed available for `make unit-test`, and its version is noted for CI.
- [ ] Any missing construct has a written workaround; if a library bump is needed it is proposed as its own change through `make update_cdk_libs`.
- [ ] No AWS resources are created and nothing is deployed.

## Blocked by

- None - can start immediately

title: 02. A poll page is live at polls.natenite.net/poll1
body:
**Type:** HITL  
**Slice:** 02

## Parent PRD

`.scratch/wayfinder/poll-app/spec.md` (decision map: `map.md`; ordered plan: `build-plan.md`; compute decision: ADR 0001)

## What to build

Thin end-to-end path for a visitor to open a poll and see its form. Adds `PollsSetting` and its per-environment JSON, a first `PollsStack` (private S3 bucket with OAC, deployment of the shared page and the poll definitions, a CloudFront distribution at the polls hostname reusing the existing certificate and attaching the existing web ACL, the viewer-request rewrite function, and the Route 53 alias), inventory wiring after the Site stack, the make targets that preview and deploy the polls stack, and the golden-test helper that ignores asset hashes. The page renders a poll's title and single-choice questions from its definition; submitting comes in slice 03.

Human gate: the first production deploy, and checking the page in a browser.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A typed `PollsSetting` loads from `config/production`, with unit tests following the existing settings tests.
- [ ] `PollsStack` is created from `PollsInput` for production and deploys after the Site stack; `cdk ls` shows `NateNiteProductionPollsStack`.
- [ ] Referencing the Site stack's web ACL adds an export to the Site stack; the regenerated Site golden file differs only by that addition.
- [ ] A golden test for the polls stack passes, and editing a poll definition or the page does not change the golden file (asset hashes are normalized by a shared test helper).
- [ ] A make target previews the polls stack diff, and another runs the unit tests and then deploys it.
- [ ] `make static` passes.
- [ ] After deploy: `https://polls.natenite.net/poll1` shows the poll and its single-choice questions; an unknown poll ID shows a 'poll not found' message; the apex and `www` sites still load.
- [ ] The page works on a phone-sized viewport.

title: 03. A single-choice poll accepts and stores a response
body:
**Type:** HITL  
**Slice:** 03

## Parent PRD

`.scratch/wayfinder/poll-app/spec.md` (decision map: `map.md`; ordered plan: `build-plan.md`; compute decision: ADR 0001)

## What to build

The first complete write path. A Python submit function validates a single-choice submission against the poll definition (bundled from the same directory that feeds the site) and writes a response record. Adds the on-demand DynamoDB table (retained, deletion protection, point-in-time recovery off), the Function URL with IAM auth reached through the distribution's submit behavior using OAC, the shared limits constants, the page's submit with the body hash header and thank-you message, and an owner script that dumps one poll's responses. Node tests join the existing test gate and CI gets a Node setup step.

Human gate: deploy and verify the signed POST path on the real distribution.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Entry-point tests with an in-memory fake table: a valid submission returns a created response and writes exactly one response record holding answers by question ID, submitted-at time and poll version; response IDs sort by submission time.
- [ ] Tests: an unknown option or a missing required answer is rejected with a machine-readable reason; an unknown poll returns not found; a body over 6 KB returns payload-too-large.
- [ ] Page logic tests (Node built-in runner) cover the body hash with a known SHA-256 vector and the request body builder.
- [ ] CI's static-check runs the Node tests with a pinned Node setup.
- [ ] Template assertions: the Function URL uses IAM auth, the table is retained with deletion protection, and the golden files are updated and read.
- [ ] An owner script dumps one poll's responses to JSON or CSV using a single query.
- [ ] After deploy: submitting through the page stores a record and shows a thank-you; a POST without the hash header fails; the raw function address is rejected; the table has the expected keys.

title: 06. Optional email stored as a separate record, with the privacy notice
body:
**Type:** AFK  
**Slice:** 06

`.scratch/wayfinder/poll-app/spec.md` (decision map: `map.md`; ordered plan: `build-plan.md`; compute decision: ADR 0001)

## What to build

Add the optional email field. When given, store it as its own record linked to the response by response ID; when omitted, store nothing. The email is never written to logs. The page shows a one-line notice that the address is kept until removal is requested (final legal wording is out of scope). Extend the owner script with 'purge emails older than N days' and 'delete by email address'.

- [ ] Entry-point tests: no email means no email record; a valid email creates an email record with the same response ID as the response; an invalid or over-254-character email is rejected with a reason.
- [ ] A test confirms no log output from the handler contains an email address.
- [ ] The page shows the optional email field and the one-line notice; skipping it works.
- [ ] The owner script purges emails older than a given age and deletes by address, with tests against the fake table.

title: 07. Poll closing time and a test that validates every poll file
body:

`.scratch/wayfinder/poll-app/spec.md` (decision map: `map.md`; ordered plan: `build-plan.md`; compute decision: ADR 0001)

## What to build

Enforce an optional closing time (UTC) on the server and show a 'poll closed' message in the page. Add a unit test that loads every real poll definition file and fails a bad one, including checking that the worst-case submission size stays within the limit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Entry-point tests with a fixed clock: a submission before the closing time is accepted; after it is rejected with a distinct reason; a poll without a closing time never closes. The status code chosen for a closed poll is documented in the tests.
- [ ] The page shows a 'poll closed' message.
- [ ] A test runs every file in the poll definitions directory and checks valid question types, unique IDs, a valid closing time, rating bounds, an integer version, and that the worst-case body (up to 4 bytes per character for every free-text cap, plus email and overhead) is under the 6 KB limit.
- [ ] A deliberately bad poll file makes the test fail (shown in the PR), and the test runs in the normal unit-test gate.
- [ ] The version number is stored on every response.

title: 09. Retry with backoff and the friendly 'busy' message
body:
**Type:** AFK  
**Slice:** 09

## Parent PRD

`.scratch/wayfinder/poll-app/spec.md` (decision map: `map.md`; ordered plan: `build-plan.md`; compute decision: ADR 0001)

## What to build

On throttled (429) and server-error responses the page retries two or three times with backoff, keeps the answers in the form, then shows a 'busy, try again in a minute' message with a one-click resubmit. Validation errors are not retried.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Node tests cover the retry decision and backoff timing: 429 and 5xx retry, 4xx validation errors do not, and the number of attempts is bounded.
- [ ] The page keeps the form filled in after a failure and offers one-click resubmit.
- [ ] The message is shown for 429, WAF blocks and 5xx alike.
- [ ] `make static` passes.

## What to build

Add the per-IP rate-based rule to the existing shared web ACL (counts only POST to the submit path on the polls hostname, 20 per 5 minutes, action block) and set the function's reserved concurrency from settings. This edits the live main-site ACL.

Human gate: review the Site diff in isolation, deploy, and run the throttling checks.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The Site golden file changes only by the new rate rule, and template assertions confirm its scope (host, path, method), limit, window and action.
- [ ] The function's reserved concurrency is read from the polls settings and asserted in the template.
- [ ] After deploy: more than 20 submit POSTs from one IP in 5 minutes are blocked; page views are not counted; driving concurrency above the cap returns HTTP 429.
- [ ] While testing, record which of Url4xxCount, Throttles and ConcurrentExecutions moved for a throttled request, and add the answer to the spec's further notes.
